newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on inflation, govt changes.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on inflation, govt changes.

text.p: Thai stocks will likely retreat on Monday on investor concerns over rising inflation and disappointment over a limited cabinet reshuffle last week, brokers said.

"Investors are worried that inflation may rise soon after the value added tax (VAT) increase. They're also concerned that the cabinet reshuffle last week would split the coalition government," said a broker.
The composite SET index lost 5.44 points to close at 623.25 on 2.4 billion baht turnover on Friday. The SET-50 index was down 0.56 to 47.
Prices of most products, except fresh foods, rose from Saturday when the VAT was increased to 10 percent from seven.

Brokers said investors had lost confidence in government stability after Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh brought in two outsiders - former finance minister Virabongsa Ramangkura and communications tycoon Thaksin Shinawatra as deputy prime ministers - to boost the sagging image of his cabinet on Friday.
